hint.description: The next step, when the server knows one.

playerToken.description: PLAYER_TOKEN from the server environment; accepted only on owner_or_player routes (library browsing, title lookup and requests, streaming).

info.description:
All /api/v1 routes except the Seerr webhook need "Authorization: Bearer <OWNER_TOKEN>".
Success bodies are {"data": ..., "meta": ...}; errors are {"error": {"code": "snake_case", "message": "..."}} with a 4xx/5xx status.
Request bodies are JSON (Content-Type: application/json) and unknown fields are rejected with 400.
Every operation has x-mm-effect: "read" (no change), "write" (changes Media Manager state or queues local work),
"provider" (contacts or queues requests to indexers, Seerr, Plex or metadata services and can spend provider budget)
or "destructive" (removes or replaces data; ask the owner first). x-mm-auth
"owner_or_player" routes also accept the player token. Workflow actions are guarded by state and revision. GET /api/v1/workflows/{id} lists available_actions (route, effect,
available or the reason why not, and a ready body). A 409 means the action does not apply right now; error.hint says what
to do instead. Background work is paced: a 202 means queued, not finished.

post.description:
For a file AltMount does not report but that plays badly (for example slow seeking because its articles come from a backup provider). altmount_file_path is the file's path as AltMount reports it, e.g. media-manager/<release>/<file>.mkv. The website also supplies file_id to bind the request to that exact current publication; a mismatched or stale ID is 404. Opens a repair (reason owner_requested) that acquires a replacement under the publication's profile, excluding the current release title; the old file keeps playing until Plex confirms the replacement. outcome is opened, attached (an open workflow already acquires that title), already_open or needs_attention (detail in GET /api/v1/repairs). 404 when the path backs no current publication, 409 while the publishing workflow is still in flight.

Never the default (409 quality_profile_is_default). Without replace_with only a profile with no workflows (finished ones included), adopted files, adoption batches, import lists or Seerr routes is deleted; otherwise 409 quality_profile_in_use. With ?replace_with=<id> of another enabled profile of the same media kind (422 quality_profile_replacement_invalid otherwise) every reference moves to that profile in the same transaction and the response reports the counts. The replacement's policy_version is raised, so moved titles whose round rules differ wait for apply-policy exactly as after a profile edit; they are never evaluated under the new rules silently. Audited as quality_profile.deleted.

post.description:
For a media kind without a default library root, uses the first ordinary (non-4K) Plex library of that kind. The folder Media Manager writes is proven, not guessed: Media Manager creates an empty marker folder (mm-opsaetning-tjek-…) in each folder it may write, asks Plex to list the library's folder, keeps the one whose marker Plex shows and removes every marker. Where Plex sees AltMount is proven by comparing the folders both list. For a kind without a default quality profile, creates "Dansk tekst eller tale" (Balanced preset, Danish subtitles or Danish speech required). Existing settings are never changed. With apply false (also creates and removes the markers) it only reports; every step that cannot be done says why.
